content.text:
## COR-2174, concisely

**What it is.** The launchd watch daemon keeps running the binary it was started with. On 2026-10-19 the nightly added a `transcript_storage` manifest field (COR-2168) without a schema bump. The still-running old daemon's writer-path manifest load (`loadBrainManifestForReplace`, `internal/cli/brain.go:203`) correctly refuses unknown fields so it won't erase another build's state — but that refusal surfaces as `memory_state_corrupt` and fails every tick forever (`internal/cli/watch.go:363` skips all agent work).

**Why fix it.** Silent total outage: distill never runs, deferred sessions pile up, and `entire brain status` still says `daemon ✓ running` — nothing restarts the daemon and nothing tells the user. Every binary upgrade reproduces it.

**Solution.** The ticket offers three directions; the right pick is the first — the daemon detects it's stale and exits so launchd relaunches it on the current binary:

- At startup, record the executable's identity (mtime or hash via `os.Executable`). Each tick, cheap re-stat; on change, log "binary upgraded, restarting" and exit cleanly.
- Also exit when the manifest unknown-field error fires (`errRetiredManifestField` already classifies it) — that's the "a newer build wrote this" signal even if the stat check misses (e.g. same path, atomic replace caught by mtime anyway).

**Why that fixes it.** It removes the root cause — a daemon outliving its binary — instead of patching the symptom: the new binary parses the new manifest fine, so one restart ends the failure loop permanently and needs no user action.

**One real complication the ticket proves:** with ad-hoc (linker-signed) binaries, launchd's launch constraint pins the old cdhash — after the binary changes, relaunch fails with `OS_REASON_CODESIGNING` until the agent is re-bootstrapped (`bootout` + `bootstrap`). So exit-and-restart alone is not enough on macOS; the fix also needs the new binary to re-bootstrap the agent, most naturally from a frequently-run CLI path (e.g. `setup`/`status`/the next `brain` command detects the daemon's plist points at a binary whose cdhash changed, or detects spawn-failed state, and re-bootstraps). The error-relabeling and status-visibility directions overlap with COR-2162, which you're reviewing separately.

If that direction works for you — daemon self-exit on binary change + CLI-side re-bootstrap to clear the codesigning pin — I'll implement it.

168	// systemdUnitName is the daemon name with the unit suffix; systemd unit names
169	// are already plain identifiers, so no transformation is needed.
170	func systemdUnitName(name string) string { return name + ".service" }
171	
172	// planBrainWatchDaemon resolves the spec against a target OS and home directory.
173	// goos/home/configHome/unitDir are parameters, not ambient state, so both
174	// platforms' artifacts are testable from one machine. A non-empty unitDir (the
175	// ENTIRE_BRAIN_DAEMON_DIR knob) replaces the service manager's directory
176	// entirely, which is what keeps a sandboxed run out of a real user's LaunchAgents.
177	func planBrainWatchDaemon(goos, home, configHome, unitDir string, spec daemonSpec) (daemonPlan, error) {
178		if strings.TrimSpace(spec.Name) == "" {
179			spec.Name = daemonDefaultName
180		}
181		if err := validateDaemonName(spec.Name); err != nil {
182			return daemonPlan{}, err
183		}
184		if strings.TrimSpace(spec.Binary) == "" {
185			return daemonPlan{}, fmt.Errorf("daemon binary path is required")
186		}
187		// A newline in any rendered value would close the line and let the rest be
188		// read as further unit directives. No escaping expresses it; refuse instead.
189		values := append([]string{spec.Binary, spec.WorkingDir, spec.LogPath}, spec.Args...)
190		for key, value := range spec.Env {
191			values = append(values, key, value)
192		}
193		for _, value := range values {
194			if !unitValueSafe(value) {
195				return daemonPlan{}, fmt.Errorf("daemon service values must not contain newlines: %q", value)
196			}
197		}
198		unitDir = strings.TrimSpace(unitDir)
199		plan := daemonPlan{OS: goos, Spec: spec}
200		switch goos {
201		case "darwin":
202			if home == "" && unitDir == "" {
203				return daemonPlan{}, fmt.Errorf("cannot resolve home directory for the launchd agent")
204			}
205			plan.Manager = daemonManagerLaunchd
206			plan.Label = launchdLabel(spec.Name) + daemonScopeSuffix(unitDir)
207			root := unitDir
208			if root == "" {
209				root = daemonPathJoin(home, "Library", "LaunchAgents")
210			}
211			plan.UnitPath = daemonPathJoin(root, plan.Label+".plist")
212			plan.Contents = renderLaunchdPlist(plan.Label, spec)
213		case "linux":
214			root := unitDir
215			if root == "" {
216				root = configHome
217				if root == "" {
218					if home == "" {
219						return daemonPlan{}, fmt.Errorf("cannot resolve config directory for the systemd user unit")
220					}
221					root = daemonPathJoin(home, ".config")
222				}
223				root = daemonPathJoin(root, "systemd", "user")
224			}
225			plan.Manager = daemonManagerSystemd
226			// Same hazard as launchd: the unit NAME is constant, so a throwaway
227			// install into an overridden directory would otherwise collide with
228			// the real unit. Fixing one platform and not the other is how the two
229			// halves drift apart.
230			plan.Label = systemdUnitName(spec.Name + strings.ReplaceAll(daemonScopeSuffix(unitDir), ".", "-"))
231			plan.UnitPath = daemonPathJoin(root, plan.Label)
232			plan.Contents = renderSystemdUnit(spec)
233		default:
234			plan.Manager = daemonManagerUnsupported
235			plan.Label = spec.Name
236		}
237		return plan, nil
238	}

240	// sortedEnvKeys keeps rendered artifacts byte-stable across runs (Go map order
241	// is randomized), which is what lets idempotence be decided by comparing the
242	// file on disk against the freshly rendered plan.
243	func sortedEnvKeys(env map[string]string) []string {
244		keys := make([]string, 0, len(env))
245		for key := range env {
246			keys = append(keys, key)
247		}
248		sort.Strings(keys)
249		return keys
250	}

252	func xmlEscape(value string) string {
253		var buf bytes.Buffer
254		_ = xml.EscapeText(&buf, []byte(value))
255		return buf.String()
256	}
257	
258	func renderLaunchdPlist(label string, spec daemonSpec) string {
259		var b strings.Builder
260		b.WriteString(`<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>` + "\n")
261		b.WriteString(`<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">` + "\n")
262		b.WriteString(`<plist version="1.0">` + "\n")
263		b.WriteString("<dict>\n")
264		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  <key>Label</key>\n  <string>%s</string>\n", xmlEscape(label))
265		b.WriteString("  <key>ProgramArguments</key>\n  <array>\n")
266		for _, arg := range append([]string{spec.Binary}, spec.Args...) {
267			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "    <string>%s</string>\n", xmlEscape(arg))
268		}
269		b.WriteString("  </array>\n")
270		if len(spec.Env) > 0 {
271			b.WriteString("  <key>EnvironmentVariables</key>\n  <dict>\n")
272			for _, key := range sortedEnvKeys(spec.Env) {
273				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "    <key>%s</key>\n    <string>%s</string>\n", xmlEscape(key), xmlEscape(spec.Env[key]))
274			}
275			b.WriteString("  </dict>\n")
276		}
277		if spec.WorkingDir != "" {
278			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  <key>WorkingDirectory</key>\n  <string>%s</string>\n", xmlEscape(spec.WorkingDir))
279		}
280		if spec.LogPath != "" {
281			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  <key>StandardOutPath</key>\n  <string>%s</string>\n", xmlEscape(spec.LogPath))
282			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  <key>StandardErrorPath</key>\n  <string>%s</string>\n", xmlEscape(spec.LogPath))
283		}
284		b.WriteString("  <key>RunAtLoad</key>\n  <true/>\n")
285		b.WriteString("  <key>KeepAlive</key>\n  <true/>\n")
286		// A crash-looping watcher must not spin: 60s between relaunches is far
287		// below the 5m tick, so a healthy daemon never notices the throttle.
288		b.WriteString("  <key>ThrottleInterval</key>\n  <integer>60</integer>\n")
289		b.WriteString("  <key>ProcessType</key>\n  <string>Background</string>\n")
290		b.WriteString("  <key>LowPriorityIO</key>\n  <true/>\n")
291		b.WriteString("</dict>\n</plist>\n")
292		return b.String()
293	}

295	// systemdQuote renders a value for systemd's quoted argument syntax. Use it
296	// ONLY for settings systemd unquotes — the ones parsed with extract_first_word
297	// (EXTRACT_UNQUOTE): ExecStart= and Environment=.
298	func systemdQuote(value string) string {
299		replacer := strings.NewReplacer(`\`, `\\`, `"`, `\"`)
300		return `"` + systemdEscapeSpecifiers(replacer.Replace(value)) + `"`
301	}
302	
303	// systemdSingleValue renders a value for a setting that takes ONE value and is
304	// NOT unquoted by systemd: WorkingDirectory=, StandardOutput=, StandardError=.
305	//
306	// Those are parsed by config_parse_working_directory / config_parse_exec_output,
307	// which run unit_path_printf on the raw right-hand side and never call
308	// extract_first_word — so a quoted path arrives with its quote characters still
309	// in it and is then rejected by path_simplify_and_warn's absolute-path check.
310	// Wrapping these in quotes does not harden them, it breaks them. Spaces need no
311	// treatment at all here: the whole rest of the line is the value.
312	//
313	// What DOES need handling is the one transformation systemd applies to them,
314	// specifier expansion: a literal % must be written %% or it is silently read as
315	// a specifier (e.g. %h expands to the home directory). Newlines cannot be
316	// represented in a unit value in any form and are rejected by the caller.
317	func systemdSingleValue(value string) string {
318		return systemdEscapeSpecifiers(value)
319	}
320	
321	func systemdEscapeSpecifiers(value string) string {
322		return strings.ReplaceAll(value, "%", "%%")
323	}
324	
325	// unitValueSafe rejects the values no unit-file escaping can express. A newline
326	// would end the line and turn the remainder into a forged directive.
327	func unitValueSafe(value string) bool {
328		return !strings.ContainsAny(value, "\n\r")
329	}

331	func renderSystemdUnit(spec daemonSpec) string {
332		var b strings.Builder
333		b.WriteString("[Unit]\n")
334		b.WriteString("Description=Entire brain watcher (deterministic refresh is free; agent steps are gated)\n")
335		b.WriteString("Documentation=https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain\n")
336		b.WriteString("After=default.target\n\n")
337		b.WriteString("[Service]\n")
338		b.WriteString("Type=simple\n")
339		exec := make([]string, 0, len(spec.Args)+1)
340		for _, arg := range append([]string{spec.Binary}, spec.Args...) {
341			exec = append(exec, systemdQuote(arg))
342		}
343		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "ExecStart=%s\n", strings.Join(exec, " "))
344		if spec.WorkingDir != "" {
345			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "WorkingDirectory=%s\n", systemdSingleValue(spec.WorkingDir))
346		}
347		for _, key := range sortedEnvKeys(spec.Env) {
348			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "Environment=%s\n", systemdQuote(key+"="+spec.Env[key]))
349		}
350		if spec.LogPath != "" {
351			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "StandardOutput=append:%s\n", systemdSingleValue(spec.LogPath))
352			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "StandardError=append:%s\n", systemdSingleValue(spec.LogPath))
353		}
354		b.WriteString("Restart=always\n")
355		b.WriteString("RestartSec=60\n")
356		b.WriteString("Nice=10\n\n")
357		b.WriteString("[Install]\n")
358		b.WriteString("WantedBy=default.target\n")
359		return b.String()
360	}

362	// daemonPathPlaceholder stands in for the inherited search path while two
363	// rendered units are compared. It is never written to disk.
364	const daemonPathPlaceholder = "\x00entire-brain-daemon-path\x00"
365	
366	// daemonUnitMaterial reduces a rendered unit to the part that decides what the
367	// daemon DOES, so `Current` answers "would this build install a different
368	// service" instead of "was this shell's environment byte-identical to the one
369	// that installed it".
370	//
371	// The only ambient value in the unit is PATH. daemonEnv copies it from the
372	// installing process because a launchd/systemd job inherits almost nothing and
373	// the deterministic refresh shells out to `git` and `entire` — but PATH is the
374	// most volatile variable on a developer machine. Installing a tool, opening a
375	// different terminal, a shell rc that prepends a directory twice: any of those
376	// made the on-disk unit differ from the freshly rendered one by a single line.
377	//
378	// Byte equality therefore reported drift on a perfectly good service, and
379	// `setup` "repairs" drift by unloading and reloading it — tearing down the ONE
380	// machine-wide watcher, mid-refresh, on a re-run that changed nothing. `status`
381	// meanwhile told the user their running watcher was stale and to re-run the
382	// command that would do it again. This is the same failure the log path caused
383	// before it was made machine-level (see brainWatchDaemonPlan); PATH is the
384	// remaining instance of it, and the more volatile one.
385	//
386	// Masking is deliberately narrow: only the PATH VALUE is neutralized. A unit
387	// that gains or loses PATH entirely, or whose binary, arguments, working
388	// directory, log path or ENTIRE_PLUGIN_* dirs changed, still reads as drift and
389	// is still repaired — and a real reinstall always writes the current PATH.
390	func daemonUnitMaterial(manager, contents string) string {
391		lines := strings.Split(contents, "\n")
392		switch manager {
393		case daemonManagerLaunchd:
394			for i, line := range lines {
395				if strings.TrimSpace(line) != "<key>PATH</key>" || i+1 >= len(lines) {
396					continue
397				}
398				next := strings.TrimSpace(lines[i+1])
399				if strings.HasPrefix(next, "<string>") && strings.HasSuffix(next, "</string>") {
400					lines[i+1] = daemonPathPlaceholder
401				}
402			}
403		case daemonManagerSystemd:
404			for i, line := range lines {
405				if strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(line), `Environment="PATH=`) {
406					lines[i] = daemonPathPlaceholder
407				}
408			}
409		default:
410			return contents
411		}
412		return strings.Join(lines, "\n")
413	}
414	
415	// setupDaemonLockName serializes the daemon REGISTRATION sequence across
416	// processes. It lives beside the machine-level watch plan, in the plugin state
417	// dir, for the same reason the plan does: exactly one service exists per
418	// machine, so the thing that guards it must be machine-level too.
419	const setupDaemonLockName = "daemon-install.lock"
420	
421	// withDaemonRegistrationLock runs fn holding the machine-level daemon lock.
422	//
423	// `setup` decides what to do about the daemon with inspect() and then acts with
424	// install()/uninstall(), and install() on darwin is not one call but two
425	// (`launchctl unload` then `launchctl load -w`) with the service DOWN in
426	// between. None of that was serialized, while the watch plan written moments
427	// earlier — the far less dangerous file — already was. Two repos onboarding at
428	// once is the ordinary case this whole file was rewritten for, and interleaving
429	// two unload/load pairs against one label means one run's `load` can land
430	// between the other's `unload` and `load`: the second then fails with "service
431	// already loaded" and `setup` reports "daemon install failed" for a watcher
432	// that is in fact running. Every process now observes the service, changes it
433	// and re-observes it as one atomic step.
434	//
435	// It degrades rather than fails: a state dir that cannot be resolved or locked
436	// runs fn unlocked, because a machine that cannot take the lock must still be
437	// able to install its watcher.
438	func withDaemonRegistrationLock(env EntireEnv, fn func() error) error {
439		planPath, err := setupWatchPlanPath(env)
440		if err != nil {
441			return fn()
442		}
443		stateDir := filepath.Dir(planPath)
444		if err := rejectExistingSymlinkPathComponents(stateDir, brainLockDirName); err != nil {
445			return fn()
446		}
447		lock, err := acquireFileLock(filepath.Join(stateDir, brainLockDirName, setupDaemonLockName), "daemon_install_locked", brainWriteLockTimeout)
448		if err != nil {
449			return fn()
450		}
451		defer func() { _ = lock.Close() }()
452		return fn()
453	}

455	// daemonState is what `setup` and `status` report about the installed watcher.
456	type daemonState struct {
457		Manager   string `json:"manager"`
458		Label     string `json:"label,omitempty"`
459		UnitPath  string `json:"unit_path,omitempty"`
460		Installed bool   `json:"installed"`
461		// Current is true when the file on disk matches what this build would
462		// write. A stale unit is "installed" but must be rewritten — that is the
463		// difference between idempotent re-run and silent drift.
464		Current bool   `json:"current"`
465		Running bool   `json:"running"`
466		Detail  string `json:"detail,omitempty"`
467	}
468	
469	// inspectDaemon reports the installed/current/running triple without changing
470	// anything. Detection is deliberately cheap: one file read plus one service
471	// manager query.
472	func inspectDaemon(ctx context.Context, runner CommandRunner, plan daemonPlan) daemonState {
473		state := daemonState{Manager: plan.Manager, Label: plan.Label, UnitPath: plan.UnitPath}
474		if !plan.supported() {
475			// Same wording setup's skip line uses, so `status` and `setup` describe
476			// one platform fact the same way instead of two apparent conditions.
477			state.Detail = "not supported on " + plan.OS + " yet (no launchd or systemd)"
478			return state
479		}
480		data, err := os.ReadFile(plan.UnitPath)
481		switch {
482		case err == nil:
483			state.Installed = true
484			state.Current = daemonUnitMaterial(plan.Manager, string(data)) == daemonUnitMaterial(plan.Manager, plan.Contents)
485		case os.IsNotExist(err):
486			// Nothing installed under this label, so nothing can be running under
487			// it either. Skipping the probe keeps `status` free of a subprocess on
488			// the overwhelmingly common not-set-up path.
489			return state
490		default:
491			state.Detail = "read unit: " + err.Error()
492			return state
493		}
494		state.Running, state.Detail = daemonRunning(ctx, runner, plan)
495		return state
496	}
497	
498	func daemonRunning(ctx context.Context, runner CommandRunner, plan daemonPlan) (bool, string) {
499		if plan.NoRegister {
500			// Never probe the live session in a no-register run: `launchctl list`
501			// against a real label would report a job this process did not install
502			// and must not claim.
503			return false, "not registered (" + envDaemonNoRegister + ")"
504		}
505		if runner == nil {
506			return false, "no command runner"
507		}
508		switch plan.Manager {
509		case daemonManagerLaunchd:
510			if _, _, err := runner.Run(ctx, "", "launchctl", "list", plan.Label); err != nil {
511				return false, ""
512			}
513			return true, ""
514		case daemonManagerSystemd:
515			stdout, _, err := runner.Run(ctx, "", "systemctl", "--user", "is-active", plan.Label)
516			// systemctl exits nonzero for every inactive state, so the stdout word
517			// is the signal, not the exit code.
518			if strings.TrimSpace(string(stdout)) == "active" {
519				return true, ""
520			}
521			if err != nil {
522				return false, ""
523			}
524			return false, ""
525		}
526		return false, ""
527	}

529	// refreshDaemonUnitBytes rewrites the unit file when it differs from what this
530	// build would install, WITHOUT going near the service manager.
531	//
532	// It is the other half of daemonUnitMaterial. Masking PATH out of the
533	// "is it current" decision correctly stops `setup` from tearing the live
534	// watcher down over a shell variable — but on its own it would also freeze the
535	// daemon's PATH at whatever the very first install happened to inherit, with
536	// nothing ever refreshing it. Writing the file here and reloading nothing gets
537	// both: the running service is left strictly alone, and it picks up the current
538	// PATH at its next natural restart (login, crash, reboot).
539	//
540	// A failure is deliberately not an error to the caller: the watcher is running
541	// and correct, and refusing a re-run of `setup` over a cosmetic rewrite would
542	// be worse than skipping it.
543	func refreshDaemonUnitBytes(plan daemonPlan) error {
544		if !plan.supported() {
545			return nil
546		}
547		data, err := os.ReadFile(plan.UnitPath)
548		if err != nil || string(data) == plan.Contents {
549			return err
550		}
551		return writeFileAtomic(plan.UnitPath, []byte(plan.Contents), 0o600)
552	}
553	
554	// installDaemon writes the unit and (re)loads it. It is idempotent by
555	// construction: the file write is unconditional-but-identical when nothing
556	// changed, and the unload-then-load pair leaves exactly one job registered no
557	// matter how many times setup runs.
558	func installDaemon(ctx context.Context, runner CommandRunner, plan daemonPlan) error {
559		if !plan.supported() {
560			return fmt.Errorf("no supported service manager for %s", plan.OS)
561		}
562		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(plan.UnitPath), 0o755); err != nil {
563			return fmt.Errorf("create service directory: %w", err)
564		}
565		if plan.Spec.LogPath != "" {
566			if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(plan.Spec.LogPath), 0o700); err != nil {
567				return fmt.Errorf("create log directory: %w", err)
568			}
569		}
570		if err := writeFileAtomic(plan.UnitPath, []byte(plan.Contents), 0o600); err != nil {
571			return fmt.Errorf("write %s: %w", plan.UnitPath, err)
572		}
573		if runner == nil || plan.NoRegister {
574			// No-register: the unit file is on disk and byte-identical to what a
575			// real install would write, and the caller's launchd/systemd session is
576			// untouched.
577			return nil
578		}
579		switch plan.Manager {
580		case daemonManagerLaunchd:
581			// Unload first so a re-run replaces a stale job instead of failing with
582			// "service already loaded" — this is the idempotence hinge on darwin.
583			_, _, _ = runner.Run(ctx, "", "launchctl", "unload", plan.UnitPath)
584			if _, stderr, err := runner.Run(ctx, "", "launchctl", "load", "-w", plan.UnitPath); err != nil {
585				return fmt.Errorf("launchctl load: %w: %s", err, strings.TrimSpace(string(stderr)))
586			}
587		case daemonManagerSystemd:
588			if _, stderr, err := runner.Run(ctx, "", "systemctl", "--user", "daemon-reload"); err != nil {
589				return fmt.Errorf("systemctl daemon-reload: %w: %s", err, strings.TrimSpace(string(stderr)))
590			}
591			if _, stderr, err := runner.Run(ctx, "", "systemctl", "--user", "enable", "--now", plan.Label); err != nil {
592				return fmt.Errorf("systemctl enable --now: %w: %s", err, strings.TrimSpace(string(stderr)))
593			}
594		}
595		return nil
596	}

598	// uninstallDaemon stops the service and removes the unit. Missing state is not
599	// an error: uninstalling twice must succeed.
600	func uninstallDaemon(ctx context.Context, runner CommandRunner, plan daemonPlan) error {
601		if !plan.supported() {
602			return nil
603		}
604		if _, err := os.Stat(plan.UnitPath); os.IsNotExist(err) {
605			return nil
606		} else if err != nil {
607			return err
608		}
609		if runner != nil && !plan.NoRegister {
610			switch plan.Manager {
611			case daemonManagerLaunchd:
612				if _, stderr, err := runner.Run(ctx, "", "launchctl", "unload", "-w", plan.UnitPath); err != nil {
613					return fmt.Errorf("launchctl unload: %w: %s", err, strings.TrimSpace(string(stderr)))
614				}
615			case daemonManagerSystemd:
616				if _, stderr, err := runner.Run(ctx, "", "systemctl", "--user", "disable", "--now", plan.Label); err != nil {
617					return fmt.Errorf("systemctl disable --now: %w: %s", err, strings.TrimSpace(string(stderr)))
618				}
619			}
620		}
621		if err := os.Remove(plan.UnitPath); err != nil && !os.IsNotExist(err) {
622			return fmt.Errorf("remove %s: %w", plan.UnitPath, err)
623		}
624		if runner != nil && !plan.NoRegister && plan.Manager == daemonManagerSystemd {
625			_, _, _ = runner.Run(ctx, "", "systemctl", "--user", "daemon-reload")
626		}
627		return nil
628	}

630	const (
631		// daemonLogMaxBytes caps the installed watcher's log before it is rotated.
632		// The watcher is a KeepAlive service meant to run for months and it prints
633		// several lines PER TICK PER REPO — plus, on a brain whose manifest cannot
634		// be parsed, three error lines every tick forever. Nothing rotated that
635		// file: not launchd (StandardOutPath is a plain append), not systemd
636		// (append: likewise), and not this program, which caps the memory worker's
637		// log at 1 MiB and the facts vitality log at 1 MiB but left the one log
638		// that grows fastest and lives longest unbounded.
639		//
640		// 4 MiB plus one archive keeps roughly a week of healthy five-minute ticks
641		// readable while bounding the whole thing at 8 MiB.
642		daemonLogMaxBytes = 4 << 20
643		// daemonLogArchiveSuffix names the single retained previous generation.
644		daemonLogArchiveSuffix = ".1"
645	)
646	
647	// daemonLogPath resolves the file the installed unit points stdout and stderr
648	// at. It is derived from the plugin state dir exactly as brainWatchDaemonPlan
649	// derives it, so the running watcher can find its own log without the unit
650	// having to tell it — which means no unit bytes change and no installed daemon
651	// is restarted to gain rotation.
652	func daemonLogPath(env EntireEnv) (string, error) {
653		dirs, err := resolvePluginDirs(env)
654		if err != nil {
655			return "", err
656		}
657		return filepath.Join(dirs.State, "logs", setupDaemonLogFile), nil
658	}
659	
660	// rotateDaemonLogIfLarge copies the log aside and truncates it IN PLACE.
661	//
662	// Truncation rather than rename is the whole point: launchd and systemd opened
663	// this file with O_APPEND before the process started and hold that descriptor
664	// for the life of the job. Renaming it would leave the service writing to the
665	// renamed inode forever and the fresh file permanently empty, so the log would
666	// appear to stop. An O_APPEND write always seeks to the end first, so after
667	// truncation the very next line lands at offset 0.
668	//
669	// Anything that is not a plain regular file is left alone, so a watcher run in
670	// a terminal, or one whose log path has been replaced with a symlink, is never
671	// touched.
672	func rotateDaemonLogIfLarge(path string, maxBytes int64) error {
673		if maxBytes <= 0 {
674			return nil
675		}
676		info, err := os.Lstat(path)
677		if err != nil {
678			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
679				return nil
680			}
681			return err
682		}
683		if !info.Mode().IsRegular() || info.Size() <= maxBytes {
684			return nil
685		}
686		data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
687		if err != nil {
688			return err
689		}
690		if err := writeFileAtomic(path+daemonLogArchiveSuffix, data, 0o600); err != nil {
691			return err
692		}
693		return os.Truncate(path, 0)
694	}
695	
696	// daemonLogMaintainer returns the per-pass upkeep for a watcher that IS the
697	// installed service, and nil for every other caller.
698	//
699	// The test is identity, not configuration: the returned closure exists only
700	// when this process's stdout is the very file the unit names. A `workspace
701	// watch` run by hand in a terminal, a test with a buffer, or a second watcher
702	// redirected somewhere else therefore cannot truncate the daemon's log — only
703	// the process actually writing to it can.
704	func daemonLogMaintainer(env EntireEnv) func() {
705		path, err := daemonLogPath(env)
706		if err != nil {
707			return nil
708		}
709		if !stdoutIsFile(path) {
710			return nil
711		}
712		return func() { _ = rotateDaemonLogIfLarge(path, daemonLogMaxBytes) }
713	}
714	
715	func stdoutIsFile(path string) bool {
716		target, err := os.Stat(path)
717		if err != nil {
718			return false
719		}
720		mine, err := os.Stdout.Stat()
721		if err != nil {
722			return false
723		}
724		return os.SameFile(mine, target)
725	}

20	// watch keeps the brain fresh automatically. Token-frugality is structural, not a quota:
21	// the deterministic refresh (sessions + semantic index + durable history reconciliation, seed agent
22	// ALWAYS "none") spends ZERO agent tokens and runs whenever the checkpoint/HEAD fingerprint changes.
23	// The ONLY token-spending
24	// work — distill and/or agent seed synthesis (--seed-agent) — is OFF by default and, when enabled, runs
25	// at most once per --distill-every, on the cheap --model/--effort, capped by --budget, and a persisted
26	// cursor means a restart never re-spends within the interval. Both token steps share the one gate, so
27	// --seed-agent is bounded exactly like --distill (it is NOT per-change spend).
28	type watchCommandOptions struct {
29		interval time.Duration
30		once     bool
31		// consolidateEvery throttles the FULL deterministic refresh (consolidation:
32		// sessions + semantic + history + clearing short-term memory). The
33		// fingerprint includes checkpoint refs, so during active agent work every
34		// turn would otherwise trigger the heavy path each tick; the per-tick
35		// short-term delta carries freshness in between. 0 = consolidate on every
36		// change (the pre-short-term behavior). A full short-term buffer always
37		// forces consolidation regardless of the interval.
38		consolidateEvery time.Duration
39		distill          bool
40		distillEvery     time.Duration
41		distillAgent     string
42		distillJobs      int
43		// distillMaxSessions caps how many NOT-YET-DISTILLED sessions one gated
44		// pass processes (0 = no cap). --distill-every and the persisted cursor
45		// bound how OFTEN the daemon spends; this is the only thing that bounds how
46		// MUCH one spend costs. Without it a supervised watcher's first gated tick
47		// distills the entire remaining corpus of every repo in the workspace —
48		// exactly the spend `setup` told the user it had capped at 25.
49		distillMaxSessions int
50		seedAgent          string
51		model              string
52		effort             string
53		// budget caps gated agent runs for the life of THIS PROCESS (distill + seed;
54		// each spends tokens); 0 = unlimited. It is not window-scoped and never
55		// resets while the process lives, which makes it the wrong guard for a
56		// supervised daemon — see brainWatchDaemonArgs, which deliberately omits it.
57		budget int
58	}
59	
60	// watchCursor persists across restarts so the daemon never re-refreshes unchanged state and never
61	// re-runs the gated agent work within --distill-every after a restart.
62	type watchCursor struct {
63		PendingSeed      bool      `json:"pending_seed,omitempty"`
64		PendingDistill   bool      `json:"pending_distill,omitempty"`
65		LastFingerprint  string    `json:"last_fingerprint"`
66		LastRefreshAt    time.Time `json:"last_refresh_at,omitempty"`
67		LastAgentSpendAt time.Time `json:"last_agent_spend_at,omitempty"`
68		// ConsolidationRepairs counts CONSECUTIVE full refreshes that ran early
69		// because the short-term delta failed. It is the backoff state for
70		// watchRepairWait: a single failure repairs promptly, a persistent one
71		// settles back to the normal consolidation cadence instead of firing the
72		// heavy refresh every tick. Reset to 0 by the first healthy delta.
73		ConsolidationRepairs int       `json:"consolidation_repairs,omitempty"`
74		LastFactsSyncAt      time.Time `json:"last_facts_sync_at,omitempty"`
75	}
76	
77	// watchRepairBackoffMax caps ConsolidationRepairs so the persisted counter stays
78	// bounded and the doubling in watchRepairWait can never overflow.
79	const watchRepairBackoffMax = 16

83	// watchSteps are the side-effecting operations of one tick. Injected so the loop's gating logic
84	// (change detection, agent interval/budget, cursor persistence) is unit-testable without running a real
85	// refresh/seed/distill. refresh is ALWAYS the free (seed-agent none) deterministic refresh; seed and
86	// distill are the gated, token-spending steps.
87	type watchSteps struct {
88		now         func() time.Time
89		fingerprint func(context.Context) string
90		// delta is the cheap short-term memory update (incremental export + overlay
91		// index of changed transcripts). It runs EVERY tick, before the change
92		// gate, so an in-flight session's turns are recallable near-real-time; the
93		// full refresh below is consolidation and is throttled by
94		// --consolidate-every unless the delta reports the buffer full.
95		delta func(context.Context) (shortTermStats, error)
96		// reconcile durably queues long-term conversation work independently of
97		// the git/checkpoint fingerprint. Exported transcripts can change while
98		// that fingerprint stays stable (for example, a late host export).
99		reconcile func(context.Context) error
100		refresh   func(context.Context) error
101		seed      func(context.Context) error
102		distill   func(context.Context) error
103		// factsSync publishes-and-pulls hosted facts (hostedFactsSyncAndPull) for
104		// the current + default branch. Nil when the surface has no hosted step;
105		// non-fatal and cursor-throttled (hostedSyncMinInterval).
106		factsSync func(context.Context) (bool, error)
107		paused    func() bool
108	}

110	// hostedSyncMinInterval throttles the hosted fact sync step across ticks: the
111	// tick interval is minutes, a team's fact churn is hours.
112	const hostedSyncMinInterval = 15 * time.Minute

114	// defaultWatchOptions are the shared defaults for `watch` and `workspace watch`.
115	func defaultWatchOptions() watchCommandOptions {
116		return watchCommandOptions{
117			interval:         5 * time.Minute,
118			consolidateEvery: 30 * time.Minute,
119			distillEvery:     24 * time.Hour,
120			// "auto", not "codex". A hardcoded vendor here was a THIRD codex default
121			// that never reached defaultRefreshAgent at all, so reordering that
122			// function alone would have left the watcher — the one unattended path
123			// that spends tokens on its own — routing repository content to codex
124			// forever. runDistill resolves "auto" on this path (distill_cmd.go), and
125			// `setup` still overrides it per workspace through the watch plan.
126			distillAgent: "auto",
127			distillJobs:  1,
128			seedAgent:    "none",
129		}
130	}

132	// bindWatchFlags registers the watch flags on a command, shared so `watch` and `workspace watch` expose
133	// the identical token-frugality controls.

135		cmd.Flags().DurationVar(&w.interval, "interval", w.interval, "Poll interval between ticks")
136		cmd.Flags().DurationVar(&w.consolidateEvery, "consolidate-every", w.consolidateEvery, "Minimum interval between full consolidations (heavy refresh); the per-tick short-term delta covers freshness in between. 0 = consolidate on every change; a full short-term buffer always consolidates")
137		cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&w.once, "once", false, "Run a single pass and exit (no daemon loop)")
138		cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&w.distill, "distill", false, "Run distill (SPENDS TOKENS) when new sessions land — gated by --distill-every + --budget")
139		cmd.Flags().DurationVar(&w.distillEvery, "distill-every", w.distillEvery, "Minimum interval between gated agent runs (distill and/or seed synthesis)")
140		cmd.Flags().StringVar(&w.distillAgent, "agent", w.distillAgent, "Agent for the distill step (used only with --distill)")
141		cmd.Flags().IntVar(&w.distillJobs, "jobs", w.distillJobs, "Parallel distill extraction jobs when --distill is enabled; reconciliation and writes remain deterministic")
142		cmd.Flags().IntVar(&w.distillMaxSessions, "max-sessions", w.distillMaxSessions, "Cap how many not-yet-distilled sessions ONE gated distill pass processes (0 = no cap). --distill-every bounds how often the daemon spends; this bounds how much each spend costs")
143		cmd.Flags().StringVar(&w.seedAgent, "seed-agent", w.seedAgent, "Agent for gated seed synthesis (SPENDS TOKENS); none = deterministic seed only. Bounded by --distill-every + --budget, NOT per-change")
144		cmd.Flags().StringVar(&w.model, "model", "", "Fast/cheap model for the gated agent steps (distill/seed)")
145		cmd.Flags().StringVar(&w.effort, "effort", "", "Reasoning effort for the gated agent steps (codex --config model_reasoning_effort=, claude --effort)")
146		cmd.Flags().IntVar(&w.budget, "budget", 0, "Cap on gated agent runs for the LIFE OF THIS PROCESS (distill + seed); 0 = unlimited. It never resets, so on a long-lived daemon --budget 1 means one run EVER, not one per window — the durable per-window guard is --distill-every + the persisted cursor. Use it only for a bounded foreground run.")
147	}

168	func runWatch(ctx context.Context, cmd *cobra.Command, opts Options, w watchCommandOptions, target string) error {
169		if w.interval <= 0 {
170			w.interval = 5 * time.Minute
171		}
172		if w.distillJobs <= 0 {
173			return fmt.Errorf("--jobs must be greater than 0")
174		}
175		now := opts.Now
176		if now == nil {
177			now = time.Now
178		}
179		repoDir, local, err := resolveLocalTargetRepoDir(ctx, opts.Runner, target)
180		if err != nil {
181			return err
182		}
183		if !local {
184			return fmt.Errorf("watch requires a local repository path: %s", target)
185		}
186		storage, err := repoStoragePaths(ctx, opts.Runner, opts.Env, repoDir)
187		if err != nil {
188			return err
189		}
190		cursorPath := filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(storage.HeadPath), "watch.json")
191		steps := watchStepsForRepo(cmd, opts, w, repoDir, now)
192		// Wire SIGINT/SIGTERM so a long-running daemon stops cleanly between ticks instead of being killed
193		// mid-refresh; this is what makes the loop's ctx-cancel paths live (the root command runs with a
194		// Background context otherwise).
195		ctx, stop := watchSignalContext(ctx)
196		defer stop()
197		fmt.Fprintf(cmd.OutOrStdout(), "[watch] %s — interval %s, distill=%v (every %s, agent=%s, jobs=%d, model=%q, max-sessions=%s, run-budget=%s)\n",
198			storage.Key, w.interval, w.distill, w.distillEvery, w.distillAgent, w.distillJobs, w.model,
199			watchCapLabel(w.distillMaxSessions), watchCapLabel(w.budget))
200		return watchLoop(ctx, cmd.OutOrStdout(), w, cursorPath, steps)
201	}

203	// watchCapLabel renders a cap where a non-positive value means "no cap".
204	//
205	// The banner printed a bare "budget=0", and 0 is the value a setup-installed
206	// watcher ALWAYS has: setup deliberately never passes --budget, because that
207	// counter is process-lifetime and never resets (see brainWatchDaemonArgs). So
208	// the one number the daemon's log offered about spend was both meaningless and
209	// easy to read as "zero allowed", while the cap that actually binds it --
210	// --max-sessions, carried per workspace in the machine watch plan -- was not
211	// printed at all.
212	func watchCapLabel(value int) string {
213		if value <= 0 {
214			return "uncapped"
215		}
216		return strconv.Itoa(value)
217	}

219	// watchSignalContext returns a context cancelled on SIGINT/SIGTERM so `watch` and `workspace watch`
220	// shut down cleanly between ticks (finish the current tick, then return) rather than dying abruptly.
221	func watchSignalContext(ctx context.Context) (context.Context, context.CancelFunc) {
222		return signal.NotifyContext(ctx, os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
223	}

225	func watchLoop(ctx context.Context, out io.Writer, w watchCommandOptions, cursorPath string, steps watchSteps) error {
226		agentCalls := 0
227		for {
228			if ctx.Err() != nil {
229				fmt.Fprintln(out, "[watch] stopping")
230				return nil
231			}
232			watchTick(ctx, out, w, cursorPath, steps, &agentCalls)
233			if w.once {
234				return nil
235			}
236			select {
237			case <-ctx.Done():
238				fmt.Fprintln(out, "[watch] stopping")
239				return nil
240			case <-time.After(w.interval):
241			}
242		}
243	}
244	
245	// watchTick runs one pass: cheap change detection, then (only on change) the free deterministic refresh,
246	// then the GATED token-spending work (seed synthesis and/or distill). agentCalls is shared across
247	// ticks/members so --budget caps total token spend across the whole run.
248	func watchTick(ctx context.Context, out io.Writer, w watchCommandOptions, cursorPath string, steps watchSteps, agentCalls *int) {
249		if steps.paused != nil && steps.paused() {
250			fmt.Fprintln(out, "[watch] paused — `entire-brain start` resumes")
251			return
252		}
253		// Short-term memory first, every tick: cheap (change detection + only
254		// changed transcripts), and it must never block or fail the tick; a delta
255		// failure just means the long-term path repairs freshness later.
256		bufferFull := false
257		// No delta step configured means there is no short-term path that could
258		// have failed, so the throttle applies at its normal cadence rather than
259		// treating every tick as a repair.
260		deltaHealthy := true
261		deltaNeedsReconcile := false
262		if steps.delta != nil {
263			stats, err := steps.delta(ctx)
264			if err != nil {
265				deltaHealthy = false
266				deltaNeedsReconcile = true
267				fmt.Fprintf(out, "[watch] short-term memory update failed (continuing): %v\n", err)
268			} else {
269				// A delta that failed to scan any transcript did NOT fully carry
270				// the new work, so it must not defer consolidation.
271				deltaHealthy = stats.Failed == 0
272				bufferFull = stats.Truncated
273				deltaNeedsReconcile = stats.Files > 0 || stats.Failed > 0 || stats.Truncated
274				fmt.Fprintf(out, "[watch] short-term memory updated (%d records from %d changed transcripts)\n", stats.Records, stats.Files)
275				if stats.Failed > 0 {
276					fmt.Fprintf(out, "[watch] short-term memory incomplete: %d transcripts failed to scan; consolidation will repair\n", stats.Failed)
277				}
278			}
279		}
280		// Delta state is itself a source-change signal. Do this before the git
281		// fingerprint gate so a changed/failed/overflowed export is never stranded
282		// in the short-term overlay waiting for an unrelated commit or restart.
283		if deltaNeedsReconcile && steps.reconcile != nil {
284			if err := steps.reconcile(ctx); err != nil {
285				fmt.Fprintf(out, "[watch] memory reconciliation failed (durable overlay retained): %v\n", err)
286			} else {
287				fmt.Fprintln(out, "[watch] long-term memory reconciliation queued")
288			}
289		}
290		cursor := loadWatchCursor(cursorPath)
291		// The hosted step pulls teammates' facts as much as it publishes local
292		// ones, so it must run on idle (no-change) ticks too — a machine that only
293		// receives would otherwise never sync. The defer below makes it run on
294		// every exit path from here down, including a failed refresh: a failed
295		// refresh never advances the main cursor, so a machine whose refresh
296		// always fails (e.g. the graph plugin is missing) takes that path on every
297		// tick and would otherwise be starved of the team's facts forever
298		// (COR-2114; a hand-placed call per return had already missed a path
299		// twice). It is token-free and throttled by its own cursor timestamp,
300		// advanced regardless of outcome so a failing hosted endpoint cannot turn
301		// every tick into an egress attempt. The success path still calls it
302		// explicitly BEFORE the agent steps — the `ran` guard makes the deferred
303		// call a no-op then — so the sync never inherits a context cancelled
304		// during a long agent step and burns its throttle window on an attempt
305		// that never happened.
306		factsSyncRan := false
307		runFactsSync := func() {
308			if factsSyncRan {
309				return
310			}
311			factsSyncRan = true
312			now := steps.now().UTC()
313			if steps.factsSync == nil || now.Sub(cursor.LastFactsSyncAt) < hostedSyncMinInterval {
314				return
315			}
316			attempted, err := steps.factsSync(ctx)
317			switch {
318			case err != nil:
319				fmt.Fprintf(out, "[watch] hosted fact sync failed (local brain unaffected): %v\n", err)
320			case attempted:
321				fmt.Fprintln(out, "[watch] hosted fact sync ran")
322			}
323			markFactsSyncAttempt(cursorPath, now)
324		}
325		defer runFactsSync()
326		fp := steps.fingerprint(ctx)
327		changed := fp != cursor.LastFingerprint || cursor.LastRefreshAt.IsZero()
328		if !changed && !(cursor.PendingSeed && w.seedAgent != "none" || cursor.PendingDistill && w.distill) {
329			fmt.Fprintln(out, "[watch] no change; nothing to do")
330			return
331		}
332		// Consolidation throttle: the fingerprint includes checkpoint refs, so an
333		// active agent session flips it every turn; without a throttle the heavy
334		// full refresh would run every tick exactly when the machine is busiest.
335		// A failed delta means nothing carried the new work, so the full refresh is
336		// the repair path and must not wait the whole interval (Bugbot PR #78),
337		// but it is throttled too, just on a shorter clock. The delta and the full
338		// refresh contend for the SAME brain write lock, so an unthrottled repair
339		// would fire the heavy path every tick for as long as the delta keeps
340		// failing, contending for the very lock that broke it. watchRepairWait
341		// escalates after one tick and then backs off to the normal cadence. An
342		// overflowed buffer still forces consolidation immediately: recall
343		// completeness is at risk, and a successful consolidation clears the
344		// overlay, so it cannot repeat the way a failing delta can. The first ever
345		// refresh always runs.
346		if changed && w.consolidateEvery > 0 && !cursor.LastRefreshAt.IsZero() && !bufferFull {
347			wait := w.consolidateEvery
348			state := "short-term memory is current"
349			if !deltaHealthy {
350				wait = watchRepairWait(w, cursor.ConsolidationRepairs)
351				state = fmt.Sprintf("short-term memory failed; repair refresh backing off after %d consecutive repairs", cursor.ConsolidationRepairs)
352			}
353			if since := steps.now().UTC().Sub(cursor.LastRefreshAt); since < wait {
354				fmt.Fprintf(out, "[watch] consolidation deferred (%s since last full refresh; due in %s; %s)\n",
355					since.Round(time.Second), (wait - since).Round(time.Second), state)
356				return
357			}
358		}
359		if changed {
360			if err := steps.refresh(ctx); err != nil {
361				// Refresh failed: do NOT spend tokens on an unrefreshed brain, and do NOT advance the cursor.
362				// The next tick retries the free refresh before attempting pending agent work.
363				fmt.Fprintf(out, "[watch] refresh failed (skipping agent work this tick): %v\n", err)
364				return
365			}
366		}
367		runFactsSync()
368		reserved, reason, err := reserveWatchAgentSpend(cursorPath, fp, w, agentCalls, steps.now().UTC(), !deltaHealthy)
369		if err != nil {
370			fmt.Fprintf(out, "[watch] cursor update failed (skipping agent work this tick): %v\n", err)
371			return
372		}
373		if changed {
374			fmt.Fprintln(out, "[watch] refreshed (deterministic, no agent tokens)")
375		}
376	
377		if !w.agentWorkEnabled() {
378			return
379		}
380		if !reserved {
381			fmt.Fprintf(out, "[watch] agent work skipped: %s\n", reason)
382			return
383		}
384		// Gated token-spending work: agent seed synthesis and/or distill, at most once per --distill-every,
385		// counted against --budget. A transient failure of one step is intentionally best-effort: we still
386		// advance the spend cursor + budget below so a failed step retries on the NEXT interval, not every
387		// tick (and a step that already burned tokens before failing can't be re-run for free).
388		pending := loadWatchCursor(cursorPath)
389		seedDone, distillDone := false, false
390		seedAttempted := false
391		if w.seedAgent != "none" && pending.PendingSeed {
392			seedAttempted = true
393			if err := steps.seed(ctx); err != nil {
394				fmt.Fprintf(out, "[watch] seed synthesis failed: %v\n", err)
395			} else {
396				seedDone = true
397				fmt.Fprintln(out, "[watch] synthesized seed (agent step; spent tokens)")
398			}
399		}
400		if w.distill && pending.PendingDistill {
401			switch err := steps.distill(ctx); {
402			case errors.Is(err, errDistillPassBusy):
403				// When distill was the only agent step, nothing was spent, so nothing
404				// may be charged. Hand the window
405				// back instead of logging "spent tokens" and going quiet until the
406				// next one — otherwise a watcher installed beside `setup`'s
407				// hours-long backfill loses its first window (and, if the backfill
408				// outlives it, every window) to a pass that never ran.
409				// A seed step attempted immediately before this may already have spent
410				// tokens even when it returned an error, so its reservation must stay.
411				if seedAttempted {
412					fmt.Fprintln(out, "[watch] distill skipped: another pass holds this brain; the spend window remains consumed by seed synthesis")
413				} else {
414					releaseWatchAgentSpend(cursorPath, cursor.LastAgentSpendAt, agentCalls)
415					fmt.Fprintln(out, "[watch] distill skipped: another pass holds this brain; the spend window was NOT consumed")
416				}
417			case errors.Is(err, errDistillDeferred):
418				fmt.Fprintln(out, "[watch] distilled capped batch; remaining sessions pending for the next spend window")
419			case err != nil:
420				fmt.Fprintf(out, "[watch] distill failed: %v\n", err)
421			default:
422				distillDone = true
423				fmt.Fprintln(out, "[watch] distilled facts (agent step; spent tokens)")
424			}
425		}
426		if err := withWatchCursorLock(cursorPath, func() error {
427			current := loadWatchCursor(cursorPath)
428			// A newer refresh owns its own pending work.
429			if current.LastFingerprint != pending.LastFingerprint || !current.LastRefreshAt.Equal(pending.LastRefreshAt) {
430				return nil
431			}
432			if seedDone {
433				current.PendingSeed = false
434			}
435			if distillDone {
436				current.PendingDistill = false
437			}
438			return saveWatchCursor(cursorPath, current)
439		}); err != nil {
440			fmt.Fprintf(out, "[watch] completion cursor update failed: %v\n", err)
441		}
442	}
443	
444	// releaseWatchAgentSpend gives back a window reserved by reserveWatchAgentSpend
445	// when the gated step turned out to do nothing at all. previous is the
446	// LastAgentSpendAt read at the top of this tick, so the cursor lands exactly
447	// where it was; the budget counter is decremented for the same reason. Failures
448	// are deliberately silent: the worst case is the pre-existing behaviour (a
449	// window charged for a no-op), and a watcher must never die on cursor
450	// bookkeeping.
451	func releaseWatchAgentSpend(cursorPath string, previous time.Time, agentCalls *int) {
452		_ = withWatchCursorLock(cursorPath, func() error {
453			cursor := loadWatchCursor(cursorPath)
454			cursor.LastAgentSpendAt = previous
455			if *agentCalls > 0 {
456				*agentCalls--
457			}
458			return saveWatchCursor(cursorPath, cursor)
459		})
460	}
461	
462	// agentWorkEnabled reports whether any token-spending step is turned on.
463	func (w watchCommandOptions) agentWorkEnabled() bool {
464		return w.distill || w.seedAgent != "none"
465	}
466	
467	// watchStepsForRepo builds the per-repo side effects the watch loop drives. refresh is ALWAYS the free
468	// (seed-agent none) deterministic refresh; seed and distill are the gated token steps. Shared by the
469	// single-repo `watch` and the workspace fan-out so both stay token-frugal the same way.
470	func watchStepsForRepo(cmd *cobra.Command, opts Options, w watchCommandOptions, repoDir string, now func() time.Time) watchSteps {
471		return watchSteps{
472			now:         now,
473			fingerprint: func(c context.Context) string { return watchFingerprint(c, opts.Runner, repoDir) },
474			delta:       func(c context.Context) (shortTermStats, error) { return watchShortTermDelta(c, cmd, opts, repoDir) },
475			reconcile: func(c context.Context) error {
476				_, warning, err := reconcileMemoryAndLaunch(c, opts, repoDir, "watch")
477				if warning != "" {
478					fmt.Fprintf(cmd.ErrOrStderr(), "warning: memory coordinator: %s\n", warning)
479				}
480				return err
481			},
482			refresh: func(c context.Context) error { return watchDeterministicRefresh(c, cmd, opts, repoDir) },
483			seed:    func(c context.Context) error { return watchSeed(c, cmd, opts, w, repoDir) },
484			distill: func(c context.Context) error { return watchDistill(c, cmd, opts, w, repoDir) },
485			factsSync: func(c context.Context) (bool, error) {
486				storage, err := repoStoragePaths(c, opts.Runner, opts.Env, repoDir)
487				if err != nil {
488					return false, err
489				}
490				branch := hostedSyncBranch(c, opts.Runner, repoDir)
491				attempted, err := hostedFactsSyncAndPull(c, cmd.ErrOrStderr(), opts, repoDir, storage, branch)
492				if err != nil {
493					return attempted, err
494				}
495				if branch != distillDefaultBranch {
496					also, err := hostedFactsSyncAndPull(c, cmd.ErrOrStderr(), opts, repoDir, storage, distillDefaultBranch)
497					return attempted || also, err
498				}
499				return attempted, nil
500			},
501			paused: func() bool { return backgroundPaused(opts.Env) },
502		}
503	}
504	
505	// markFactsSyncAttempt persists the hosted-sync throttle timestamp. Failures
506	// are silent for the same reason as releaseWatchAgentSpend: a watcher must
507	// never die on cursor bookkeeping.
508	func markFactsSyncAttempt(cursorPath string, now time.Time) {
509		_ = withWatchCursorLock(cursorPath, func() error {
510			cursor := loadWatchCursor(cursorPath)
511			cursor.LastFactsSyncAt = now
512			return saveWatchCursor(cursorPath, cursor)
513		})
514	}
515	
516	// watchShortTermDelta runs the short-term memory path for one repo: quiet
517	// (output discarded; the tick logs one summary line), deterministic, and
518	// token-free. The returned stats let the tick escalate to consolidation when
519	// the buffer overflows.
520	func watchShortTermDelta(ctx context.Context, cmd *cobra.Command, opts Options, repoDir string) (shortTermStats, error) {
521		perRepo := opts
522		perRepo.Env.RepoRoot = repoDir
523		deltaCmd := &cobra.Command{Use: "delta"}
524		deltaCmd.SetOut(io.Discard)
525		deltaCmd.SetErr(io.Discard)
526		deltaCmd.SetContext(ctx)
527		return runRefreshDeltaStats(deltaCmd, perRepo, true)
528	}
529	
530	// watchShouldSpend decides whether the token-spending agent work (seed and/or distill) runs this tick:
531	// only when at least one is enabled AND --distill-every has elapsed since the last agent spend
532	// (cursor-tracked across restarts) AND the --budget cap is not yet reached. This is the structural
533	// token-frugality guarantee — it bounds seed synthesis exactly like distill.
534	func watchShouldSpend(w watchCommandOptions, cursor watchCursor, agentCalls int, now time.Time) (bool, string) {
535		if !w.agentWorkEnabled() {
536			return false, "no agent steps enabled"
537		}
538		if !(cursor.LastAgentSpendAt.IsZero() || now.Sub(cursor.LastAgentSpendAt) >= w.distillEvery) {
539			return false, "--distill-every not elapsed"
540		}
541		if w.budget > 0 && agentCalls >= w.budget {
542			return false, fmt.Sprintf("--budget %d reached", w.budget)
543		}
544		return true, ""
545	}
546	
547	// watchRepairWait is the minimum time between full consolidations while the
548	// short-term delta is failing. It starts at one tick (a transient delta failure
549	// repairs on the very next pass) and doubles per consecutive repair up to the
550	// normal --consolidate-every, so a persistently failing delta degrades to the
551	// ordinary consolidation cadence instead of thrashing the shared brain write
552	// lock on every tick.
553	func watchRepairWait(w watchCommandOptions, repairs int) time.Duration {
554		wait := w.interval
555		if wait <= 0 {
556			wait = time.Minute
557		}
558		if repairs > watchRepairBackoffMax {
559			repairs = watchRepairBackoffMax
560		}
561		for i := 0; i < repairs && wait < w.consolidateEvery; i++ {
562			wait *= 2
563		}
564		if wait > w.consolidateEvery {
565			wait = w.consolidateEvery
566		}
567		return wait
568	}
569	
570	// reserveWatchAgentSpend advances the refresh cursor after a successful full
571	// refresh and decides whether the gated token work may run. repair reports
572	// whether THIS refresh ran early because the short-term delta failed; it drives
573	// the watchRepairWait backoff and is cleared by the first healthy delta.
574	func reserveWatchAgentSpend(cursorPath, fingerprint string, w watchCommandOptions, agentCalls *int, now time.Time, repair bool) (bool, string, error) {
575		var cursor watchCursor
576		var reserved bool
577		var reason string
578		err := withWatchCursorLock(cursorPath, func() error {
579			cursor = loadWatchCursor(cursorPath)
580			changed := fingerprint != cursor.LastFingerprint || cursor.LastRefreshAt.IsZero()
581			if changed {
582				cursor.PendingSeed = cursor.PendingSeed || w.seedAgent != "none"
583				cursor.PendingDistill = cursor.PendingDistill || w.distill
584				cursor.LastFingerprint = fingerprint
585				cursor.LastRefreshAt = now
586				if repair {
587					if cursor.ConsolidationRepairs < watchRepairBackoffMax {
588						cursor.ConsolidationRepairs++
589					}
590				} else {
591					cursor.ConsolidationRepairs = 0
592				}
593			}
594			if !w.agentWorkEnabled() {
595				if changed {
596					return saveWatchCursor(cursorPath, cursor)
597				}
598				return nil
599			}
600			ok, skipReason := watchShouldSpend(w, cursor, *agentCalls, now)
601			if !ok {
602				reason = skipReason
603				if changed {
604					return saveWatchCursor(cursorPath, cursor)
605				}
606				return nil
607			}
608			cursor.LastAgentSpendAt = now
609			*agentCalls++
610			reserved = true
611			return saveWatchCursor(cursorPath, cursor)
612		})
613		return reserved, reason, err
614	}
615	
616	func withWatchCursorLock(cursorPath string, fn func() error) error {
617		root := filepath.Dir(cursorPath)
618		if info, err := os.Lstat(root); err == nil && info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
619			return fmt.Errorf("watch cursor directory must not be a symlink: %s", root)
620		} else if err != nil && !os.IsNotExist(err) {
621			return err
622		}
623		if err := rejectExistingSymlinkPathComponents(root, brainLockDirName); err != nil {
624			return err
625		}
626		lock, err := acquireFileLock(filepath.Join(root, brainLockDirName, watchCursorLockName), "watch_locked", brainWriteLockTimeout)
627		if err != nil {
628			return err
629		}
630		defer func() { _ = lock.Close() }()
631		return fn()
632	}
633	
634	// watchFingerprint is a token-free change signal: the local checkpoint ref, the fetched (origin)
635	// checkpoint ref, and the worktree HEAD. Including the origin ref means a `git fetch` that brings in
636	// checkpoint activity from elsewhere also triggers a refresh. When all are unchanged since the cursor,
637	// there is nothing new to ingest.
638	func watchFingerprint(ctx context.Context, runner CommandRunner, repoDir string) string {
639		rev := func(ref string) string {
640			if runner == nil {
641				return ""
642			}
643			out, _, err := runner.Run(ctx, repoDir, "git", "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", ref)
644			if err != nil {
645				return ""
646			}
647			return strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
648		}
649		return rev(v1MainRef) + ":" + rev(v1OriginRef) + ":" + rev("HEAD")
650	}
651	
652	// watchDeterministicRefresh refreshes sessions + semantic state with the seed
653	// agent ALWAYS "none", then durably reconciles long-term conversation work.
654	// The coordinator owns projection publication, retries, and crash recovery;
655	// watch only nudges it. Agent seed synthesis remains a separate gated step.
656	func watchDeterministicRefresh(ctx context.Context, cmd *cobra.Command, opts Options, repoDir string) error {
657		return watchDeterministicRefreshComponents(ctx, cmd, opts, repoDir, watchTickBuildsHistoryProjection, false, nil)
658	}
659	
660	// watchDeterministicRefreshComponents runs the free refresh with explicit failure
661	// policy and an optional outcome observer. Setup chooses best effort; ticks fail fast.
662	//
663	// historyIndex separates the two callers that were previously identical. A
664	// watch TICK passes false: it runs every few minutes, the per-tick delta
665	// already makes new conversations recallable, and the coordinator consolidates
666	// the durable projection on its own schedule. `setup` passes true, because it
667	// is a one-shot onboarding build (the same shape as a manual `refresh`, which
668	// has always defaulted history on) and it ends by telling the user to run
669	// `entire-brain brief`. With history unbuilt that brief silently drops its
670	// transcript half and prints "history index missing" instead — setup's own
671	// recommended next command, answering with a warning about setup's own output.
672	// watchDeterministicRefreshOptions is the free path's refresh configuration,
673	// built here rather than inline so both callers' intent — above all whether the
674	// history projection is built — is readable and testable in one place.
675	func watchDeterministicRefreshOptions(historyIndex bool) refreshCommandOptions {
676		return refreshCommandOptions{
677			outputDir:       defaultExportDir,
678			checkpointLimit: defaultCheckpointLimit,
679			entireBinary:    "entire",
680			graphBinary:     "entire",
681			scope:           exportScopeAll,
682			// A tick must not bypass the durable work ledger: the per-tick delta
683			// already makes new conversations recallable while the coordinator
684			// consolidates asynchronously. A one-shot onboarding build has no next
685			// tick to wait for, so `setup` asks for it explicitly.
686			historyIndex: historyIndex,
687			semantic:     true,
688			seed: seedCommandOptions{
689				includeTests:       true,
690				maxFileBytes:       defaultSeedMaxFileBytes,
691				maxFiles:           defaultSeedMaxFiles,
692				format:             "markdown+json",
693				agent:              "none", // free: deterministic seed only; agent seed is gated via watchSeed
694				agentQuickTimeout:  2 * time.Minute,
695				agentDeepTimeout:   10 * time.Minute,
696				agentTimeoutAction: "keep-quick",
697				agentMaxInputBytes: defaultAgentMaxInput,
698			},
699		}
700	}
701	
702	func watchDeterministicRefreshComponents(ctx context.Context, cmd *cobra.Command, opts Options, repoDir string, historyIndex, bestEffort bool, component func(name string, err error)) error {
703		perRepo := opts
704		perRepo.Env.RepoRoot = repoDir
705		refreshOpts := watchDeterministicRefreshOptions(historyIndex)
706		refreshOpts.component = component
707		refreshOpts.bestEffort = bestEffort
708		sub := &cobra.Command{}
709		sub.SetContext(ctx)
710		sub.SetOut(cmd.OutOrStdout())
711		sub.SetErr(cmd.ErrOrStderr())
712		if err := runRefresh(ctx, sub, perRepo, refreshOpts); err != nil {
713			return err
714		}
715		// Deterministic and token-free, like everything else in this step: index any
716		// checkpoint commits that landed since the entity index's high-water mark.
717		// Bounded and failure-silent — a missing `entire graph` provider must never
718		// fail a tick that otherwise refreshed the brain. Under a reporter it is one
719		// more degradable component, so `setup --json`, `status` and `doctor` can
720		// name it instead of losing the reason to a discarded stderr line; with no
721		// reporter the strict watch path keeps its warning and carries on exactly as
722		// before.
723		entityErr := refreshEntityIndexQuietly(ctx, perRepo, repoDir)
724		switch {
725		case component != nil:
726			component(brainComponentEntities, entityErr)
727		case entityErr != nil:
728			fmt.Fprintf(cmd.ErrOrStderr(), "warning: entity index refresh skipped: %v\n", entityErr)
729		}
730		_, warning, err := reconcileMemoryAndLaunch(ctx, perRepo, repoDir, "watch")
731		if warning != "" {
732			fmt.Fprintf(cmd.ErrOrStderr(), "warning: memory coordinator: %s\n", warning)
733		}
734		if component != nil {
735			component(brainComponentMemory, err)
736		}
737		if bestEffort {
738			return nil
739		}
740		return err
741	}
742	
743	// watchSeed is the GATED agent seed synthesis step: it re-synthesizes the seed on the cheap --model/
744	// --effort using --seed-agent, run at most once per --distill-every and counted against --budget (see
745	// watchShouldSpend). Reuses runSeed; --update refreshes the existing seed in place.
746	func watchSeed(ctx context.Context, cmd *cobra.Command, opts Options, w watchCommandOptions, repoDir string) error {
747		seedOpts := seedCommandOptions{
748			update:             true,
749			includeTests:       true,
750			maxFileBytes:       defaultSeedMaxFileBytes,
751			maxFiles:           defaultSeedMaxFiles,
752			format:             "markdown+json",
753			agent:              w.seedAgent,
754			model:              w.model,
755			effort:             w.effort,
756			agentQuickTimeout:  2 * time.Minute,
757			agentDeepTimeout:   10 * time.Minute,
758			agentTimeoutAction: "keep-quick",
759			agentMaxInputBytes: defaultAgentMaxInput,
760		}
761		sub := &cobra.Command{}
762		sub.SetContext(ctx)
763		sub.SetOut(cmd.OutOrStdout())
764		sub.SetErr(cmd.ErrOrStderr())
765		return runSeed(ctx, sub, opts, seedOpts, repoDir)
766	}
767	
768	// errDistillPassBusy reports that the gated distill did NOTHING because another
769	// process already held the brain's distill pass lock. `distill` itself treats
770	// that as success — someone else is doing the work — but the watcher must not:
771	// it had already reserved the --distill-every window, so a silent success burned
772	// a whole window (24h by default) on a no-op and logged "spent tokens". `setup`
773	// creates that collision by design, spawning an hours-long detached backfill and
774	// installing a watcher that ticks immediately after.
775	var errDistillPassBusy = errors.New("another distill pass holds this brain")
776	
777	// errDistillDeferred retains pending work after a capped successful pass.
778	var errDistillDeferred = errors.New("distill has budget-deferred sessions")
779	
780	func watchDistill(ctx context.Context, cmd *cobra.Command, opts Options, w watchCommandOptions, repoDir string) error {
781		distillOpts := watchDistillOptions(w)
782		busy := false
783		deferred := false
784		distillOpts.onDeferredSessions = func(n int) { deferred = n > 0 }
785		distillOpts.onPassSkipped = func() { busy = true }
786		sub := &cobra.Command{}
787		sub.SetContext(ctx)
788		sub.SetOut(cmd.OutOrStdout())
789		sub.SetErr(cmd.ErrOrStderr())
790		if err := runDistill(ctx, sub, opts, distillOpts, repoDir); err != nil {
791			return err
792		}
793		if busy {
794			return errDistillPassBusy
795		}
796		if deferred {
797			return errDistillDeferred
798		}
799		return nil
800	}
801	
802	func watchDistillOptions(w watchCommandOptions) distillCommandOptions {
803		jobs := w.distillJobs
804		if jobs <= 0 {
805			jobs = 1
806		}
807		// A negative cap is a typo, not "unlimited". Only an explicit 0 means that.
808		maxSessions := w.distillMaxSessions
809		if maxSessions < 0 {
810			maxSessions = 0
811		}
812		return distillCommandOptions{
813			agent:               w.distillAgent,
814			model:               w.model,
815			effort:              w.effort,
816			timeout:             defaultDistillTimeout,
817			maxChunkBytes:       defaultDistillChunkSize,
818			confidenceThreshold: defaultFactConfidenceThreshold,
819			// The per-pass VOLUME cap. A capped pass is ordered newest-first,
820			// matching what `setup` says it did and what a reader wants first; the
821			// deferred remainder stays UNCACHED, so the next window picks it up
822			// rather than it being skipped forever. Ordering is left alone when
823			// there is no cap, so an uncapped `watch --distill` is unchanged.
824			maxSessions: maxSessions,
825			newestFirst: maxSessions > 0,
826			jobs:        jobs,
827			// concurrency is what the distill pipeline (and runDistill's guard)
828			// actually reads; --jobs is only its compatibility alias. Leaving it at
829			// the zero value made every gated distill the watcher ever attempted
830			// fail with "--concurrency must be greater than 0" before making a
831			// single agent call.
832			concurrency: jobs,
833		}
834	}
835	
836	func loadWatchCursor(path string) watchCursor {
837		var c watchCursor
838		data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
839		if err != nil {
840			return c
841		}
842		_ = json.Unmarshal(data, &c)
843		return c
844	}
845	
846	func saveWatchCursor(path string, c watchCursor) error {
847		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o700); err != nil {
848			return err
849		}
850		data, err := json.MarshalIndent(c, "", "  ")
851		if err != nil {
852			return err
853		}
854		return writeFileAtomic(path, append(data, '\n'), 0o600)
855	}

input.command: grep -rn "inspectDaemon\|installDaemon\|uninstallDaemon\|brainWatchDaemonPlan\|refreshDaemonUnitBytes" internal/cli/*.go | grep -v _test; echo ===; grep -rn "workspace watch\|runWorkspaceWatch\|newWorkspaceWatch" internal/cli/*.go | grep -v _test | head; echo ===; ls scripts/ | head -20
input.description: Find daemon plan/install call sites and workspace watch

result.output:
1554	// brainWatchDaemonPlan describes the ONE machine-wide watcher. It watches the
1555	// workspace, not this repo, so a second `setup` in a second repo adds a member
1556	// rather than a second daemon.
1557	//
1558	// Nothing in the rendered unit may depend on which repo ran setup. The log path
1559	// used to: it pointed inside the calling repo's state directory, so setting up a
1560	// second repo produced different bytes for the same machine-wide job, which
1561	// inspectDaemon correctly read as drift and "repaired" by unloading and
1562	// reloading the running daemon — every single time.
1563	func brainWatchDaemonPlan(opts Options, setupOpts setupCommandOptions) (daemonPlan, error) {
1564		return brainWatchDaemonPlanFor(runtime.GOOS, opts, setupOpts)
1565	}
1566	
1567	// brainWatchDaemonPlanFor is brainWatchDaemonPlan with the target OS as an
1568	// argument. runtime.GOOS is read in exactly one place (above) so that the whole
1569	// plan — spec, label, unit path, rendered contents — can be built for darwin or
1570	// linux from any host, which is what makes the daemon behaviour testable on a
1571	// windows runner instead of silently untested there.
1572	func brainWatchDaemonPlanFor(goos string, opts Options, setupOpts setupCommandOptions) (daemonPlan, error) {
1573		binary, err := os.Executable()
1574		if err != nil {
1575			return daemonPlan{}, fmt.Errorf("resolve executable: %w", err)
1576		}
1577		home, err := os.UserHomeDir()
1578		if err != nil {
1579			return daemonPlan{}, fmt.Errorf("resolve home directory: %w", err)
1580		}
1581		dirs, err := resolvePluginDirs(opts.Env)
1582		if err != nil {
1583			return daemonPlan{}, fmt.Errorf("resolve plugin state dir: %w", err)
1584		}
1585		spec := daemonSpec{
1586			Name:       setupOpts.daemonName,
1587			Binary:     binary,
1588			Args:       brainWatchDaemonArgs(setupOpts),
1589			WorkingDir: filepath.Dir(binary),
1590			LogPath:    filepath.Join(dirs.State, "logs", setupDaemonLogFile),
1591			Env:        daemonEnv(opts.Env),
1592		}
1593		plan, err := planBrainWatchDaemon(goos, home, os.Getenv(xdgConfigHome), os.Getenv(envDaemonUnitDir), spec)
1594		if err != nil {
1595			return daemonPlan{}, err
1596		}
1597		// Read the no-register decision ONCE, here, so install, uninstall and the
1598		// running-probe all act on the same answer for the life of this command.
1599		plan.NoRegister = daemonRegistrationDisabled()
1600		return plan, nil
1601	}
1602	
1603	// brainWatchDaemonArgs are the argv of the ONE machine-wide watcher, and they
1604	// are deliberately CONSTANT: `workspace watch --distill`, with no positional
1605	// workspace and no tuning flags. Nothing about which repo ran `setup` reaches
1606	// the unit file.
1607	//
1608	// That is the whole point. The launchd label and systemd unit name derive from
1609	// the daemon NAME alone, so they are machine-wide — but the args used to be
1610	// per-repo (`workspace watch <ws> --interval ... --model ...`). Two repos that
1611	// asked for two different workspaces resolved to the SAME unit path and rendered
1612	// DIFFERENT bytes: the second `setup` overwrote the first repo's watcher, the
1613	// first repo was never watched again, and its `status` still said "running"
1614	// because the drift was computed and then dropped. Even two repos on the SAME
1615	// workspace clobbered each other's interval, model and effort.
1616	//
1617	// With a constant unit, everything that varies per workspace — interval,
1618	// distill cadence, agent, model, effort, session cap — lives in the machine-level
1619	// watch plan (setup_watchplan.go) that the running daemon re-reads on every
1620	// outer pass. A second repo's `setup` adds a row to that plan; the unit's bytes
1621	// do not change, so inspectDaemon sees no drift and the service is never
1622	// unloaded and reloaded under an in-flight refresh.
1623	//
1624	// --distill stays here rather than in the plan because it is not tuning: it is
1625	// the statement that this service is allowed to spend at all, and `setup` always
1626	// installs a watcher that is. How MUCH and how OFTEN it may spend are both in
1627	// the plan (--max-sessions, --distill-every) and both bind, per workspace.
1628	//
1629	// --budget is deliberately NOT passed. It counts gated agent runs for the life
1630	// of the PROCESS and never resets, and this daemon is a KeepAlive service that
1631	// is meant to run for months — so `--budget 1` did not mean "one run per window",
1632	// it meant one run EVER, machine-wide, across every repo in the workspace. The
1633	// durable, self-resetting guard is the pair watch.go documents: --distill-every
1634	// plus each repo's persisted cursor, which survives restarts and bounds spend
1635	// per repo per window without ever latching off.
1636	func brainWatchDaemonArgs(setupCommandOptions) []string {
1637		return []string{"workspace", "watch", "--distill"}
1638	}
1639	
1640	func daemonEnv(env EntireEnv) map[string]string {
1641		values := map[string]string{}
1642		for key, value := range map[string]string{
1643			envPluginConfigDir: env.PluginConfigDir,

387			return runWorkspaceWatchPass(ctx, cmd, opts, pass, workspaceName, now, agentCalls)
388		}
389		return supervisedWatchLoop(ctx, cmd.OutOrStdout(), opts.Env, w, onePass, daemonLogMaintainer(opts.Env))

**COR-2174 fixed and committed** (`42387ea0` on `cor-2174-watch-daemon-wedged`, 9 files, +331/−37).

What changed:

- **Daemon self-restart** (`internal/cli/watch_binary.go`, `workspace.go`): the supervised loop probes its executable every pass (inode + mtime + size) and exits with a clear log line when it was replaced. The probe only runs when the process is the installed service (reuses the stdout-is-the-unit-log identity test), so foreground runs are untouched.
- **Codesigning pin cleared**: before exiting on macOS, the daemon spawns a detached `launchctl bootout → enable → bootstrap` helper — plain exit would hit launchd's pinned cdhash (`OS_REASON_CODESIGNING`). On Linux, exit alone suffices (`Restart=always`).
- **`installDaemon`/`uninstallDaemon`** switched from legacy `unload`/`load -w` to `bootout`/`enable`/`bootstrap`, so a plain `setup` also heals a wedged machine. `enable` covers labels an older build's `unload -w` left disabled.
- **Honest liveness probe**: `launchctl list <label>` exits 0 for a registered-but-dead job, so `daemonRunning` now requires a PID entry. This fixes the "daemon ✓ running while every spawn failed" half of the ticket and makes setup's idempotence check fall through to a reinstall exactly in the wedged state. (This also overlaps COR-2162.)

- Residual gap: if the daemon *crashes* after an upgrade but before its next pass, launchd's stale pin still blocks respawn until `setup` runs or next login. Accepted as rare; the upgrade path itself is now self-healing.

Fixes COR-2174.

## Why

The installed watcher outlives the binary it was started from. After a rebuild, the old daemon's writer-path manifest load correctly refuses fields the new build added (`json: unknown field "transcript_storage"`), so every tick fails forever — distill never runs — while `entire brain status` still says `daemon ✓ running`. Restarting isn't enough on macOS either: launchd pins the cdhash of the ad-hoc-signed binary at registration, so after an upgrade every respawn fails with `OS_REASON_CODESIGNING` until the agent is re-registered.

## What changed

- The supervised loop probes its executable (inode + mtime + size) at the top of every pass and exits with a clear log line when it was replaced; the service manager then restarts it on the current build. The probe is active only for the installed service (stdout-is-the-unit-log identity test), so foreground `workspace watch` runs keep their behavior.
- Before exiting on darwin, the daemon re-registers itself through a detached `launchctl bootout` → `enable` → `bootstrap` helper — the sequence verified to re-record launchd's cdhash pin. On linux a plain exit suffices (`Restart=always`).
- `installDaemon`/`uninstallDaemon` switched from legacy `unload`/`load -w` to `bootout`/`enable`/`bootstrap`, so a plain `setup` also heals a wedged machine. `enable` clears the disabled flag an older build's `unload -w` may have recorded.
- `daemonRunning` now requires a PID entry in `launchctl list <label>` output: a registered-but-dead job (the wedged state) lists successfully, and equating registration with running is what hid the outage. `status` now reports "installed but not running", and setup's idempotence check falls through to a reinstall exactly then. Overlaps COR-2162.

## Validation

- New tests: binary-change probe (rewrite, rename-over, mid-replace vanish), supervised-loop exit on a stale binary, PID-based liveness.
- Full `go test ./...` passes; `gofmt -s` / `go vet` clean; windows and linux cross-builds OK.
- Not exercised here: the live launchd bootout/bootstrap sequence (tests use a fake runner); it is the workaround verified by hand in COR-2174.

## Known residual gap

If the daemon crashes after an upgrade but before its next pass, launchd's stale pin still blocks respawn until `setup` runs or the next login. Accepted as rare; the upgrade path itself is now self-healing.
